\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\footnotesize Steps in the units shown; intervals are 95\% intervals and \(p\) values are from the bias-corrected test. The supremum columns give the p value of the scan over all admissible years (Methods); in panel (a) they are the supremum p values of the family of scans. In panel (c) the jump and the slope change of the two-line fit are conditional on the year 1979, and the \(p\) value of the jump is a fixed-year value. The scan of panel (c) fits a hinge and a jump at each of 35 candidate years from 1962 to 1996, with \(\Fovs\) sup-\(F\) $16.01$ at 1979 and $14.91$ at 1976; its 95\% critical value from 4{,}000 simulated AR(1) series with the bias-corrected lag-one coefficient of the full-record trend fit is $17.26$, so the break is not resolved at the 5\% level. Panel (d) gives the Holm-adjusted p values across the three variables of the first family. Panel (f) is the fit register of the step specifications: its estimate, interval and p value are those of the fitted term, and the last column gives the effective sample size of that term; the transport-share rows give the share of the trend in per cent with its sieve interval. The Argo-era rows use the section \(\Fovs\) series of ORAS5 and GLORYS12V1.\end{minipage}
